flag.summary: Paint-level opacity on a variable-bound paint does not propagate to INSTANCES. Masters render correctly; every instance renders at full opacity.
flag.detail: Known already: structural operations discard paint-level opacity, so it must be applied last. NEW and worse: even when the master reads the correct opacity, a freshly created instance reads 1. Verified on Table / Row State=Selected — master 0.08, instance 1 — and confirmed unfixable by re-creating the instance or by resetOverrides.
flag.fix: Put the alpha in the VARIABLE instead of the paint. A variable whose stored value carries its own alpha channel propagates to instances correctly. Demonstrated with color/computed (no palette)/rowSelected = rgba(0,72,82,0.08): master 0.08, instance 0.08, still bound, still zero unbound paints.
knownAffected: Chip — 18 alpha paints: Default/Hover at action.selected 12%, Outlined Secondary and Warning borders at 70% and their 4% hovers. Masters correct, instances will render solid.
Checkbox, Radio — hover ripple halos at alpha(primary.main, 0.04).
Alert, Menu, Autocomplete — no paint-level alpha; these use variables that already carry their own alpha (action.disabled, substrate/inputOutline) and are NOT affected.
flag.status: CLOSED 2026-08-02 by the alpha-to-variable remediation pass — see remediation below.

remediation.sweep: File-wide enumeration rather than the known list: 48 paints across 12 distinct (variable, opacity) combinations. The known list was INCOMPLETE — outlined Chip borders at 70% exist for error, info and success as well as secondary and warning, and the Dialog reference frame's scrim at 50% was unlisted.
remediation.namingRule: Named for the FORMULA — which colour at what alpha — not for the consuming component. alphaPrimary04 is shared by Checkbox, Radio and Switch: Switch's rule is alpha(action.active, 0.04) and the others use alpha(primary.main, 0.04), and paletteValues.ts gives both the same literal #004852. The variable description records that if those two palette entries ever diverge, this variable must split.
remediation.instanceVerification: 49 instance paints checked by instantiating every affected variant and comparing the RENDERED paint — colour, effective alpha and bound variable — against its master. 0 mismatches. Master-level reads were explicitly not accepted as evidence.
remediation.alsoFound: The widened audit surfaced 3 unbound paints that every previous audit had missed, in the Radio DO NOT USE reference frame's orphan glyph. Prior audits walked component sets only, never reference frames. Both the paints and the audit scope are fixed.

flag.whyItWasMissed: Every prior audit measured MASTERS. Reference frames built from instances existed for Menu, Radio, Button group and Dialog, but none of those used a paint-level alpha, so the divergence never rendered until the Table reference frame put an alpha row in an instance.

flag.summary: Contained groups get NO negative margin, so the join is two full 1px borders; Tebra resolves it differently per colour.
flag.detail: MUI's marginLeft: -1 seam collapse is scoped to `variant === 'outlined'` only (ButtonGroup.js lastButton/middleButton block). Tebra's ButtonGroupOverrides sets defaultProps variant 'contained', so no group in this library gets the collapse — adjacent segments sit flush and the join is the left segment's right border plus the right segment's left border.

resolved.primary: groupedContainedPrimary sets `&:not(:last-of-type) { borderColor: core.main; borderRightColor: transparent }` — the left segment's right border disappears, leaving the next segment's core.main left border as a single 1px sage line.
resolved.secondary: groupedContainedSecondary sets `&:not(:last-of-type) { borderColor: secondary.main; borderRightColor: primary.main }` — a teal right border against the next segment's coral left border, reading as a 1px teal divider. Drawn in Figma as a 1px Seam rectangle, because Figma cannot colour one side of a stroke independently.
resolved.disabledNonLast: groupedContainedHorizontal's `&:not(:last-child):disabled { borderRightColor: transparent }` carries higher specificity than groupedContainedPrimary's `&:disabled { borderColor: core.main }`, so the right border stays transparent. For secondary, groupedContainedSecondary resolves last in the overridesResolver and sets borderRightColor primary[200], which wins.

flag.radii: Button's radius 24 is kept on the outer ends only: first loses its right radii, last its left, middle all four. 24 still clamps to height/2, so end caps read as pill halves at 15 / 19 / 21. Tebra does not override the group radius; ButtonGroupRoot's own shape.borderRadius 4 is invisible because the container has no fill or border.

flag.summary: The TextField story's two multiline examples are labelled backwards, and rows='grow' has no implementation anywhere in the checkout.
flag.detail: InputBase branches: `if (rows) { inputProps = {minRows: rows, maxRows: rows, ...} }` and BOTH branches then set InputComponent = TextareaAutosize. So `multiline` alone auto-grows, and `rows={n}` pins the height. The story labels the no-rows example 'Default Fixed Height in Rows' (it actually grows) and the rows='grow' example 'Original Multiline Height Behavior' (the string is fed into minRows/maxRows height arithmetic). grep for 'grow' across packages/design-system returns only the story itself — there is no patch implementing it.
flag.handling: RESOLVED as a process item — logged to the web-app-v2 bug list as item five (story documentation contradicts InputBase behaviour; the implied grow implementation does not exist in the checkout). The Figma model stays a static 3-row boolean, which is correct for a component library, and the component description states the real behaviour in one line so the story labels are not read as authoritative.

flag.summary: The nav bar renders 65px, not 64px — the discovery pass recorded 64 and wrongly dismissed the legacy library's 65.
flag.where: navigation-ui/src/components/Navigation/Navigation.tsx Toolbar sx minHeight:64, against design-system/src/cobranding/createPartnerTheme.ts MuiIconButton.styleOverrides.sizeLarge { height: "65px", width: "65px" }.
flag.detail: minHeight is a floor, not a fixed height. The Toolbar is display:flex with align-items:center and no height cap, so a 65px child expands it. Every top-level nav item and every right-cluster utility is an IconButton at size='large', so the 65px always applies and the bar is always 65px. flag.correctsFlag: components.PrimaryNavBar crossReference, which claimed 65 was a legacy-library value rather than source.
flag.whyItWasMissed: The discovery pass read Navigation.tsx for the bar and NavIconButton.tsx for the button, but took sizeLarge from neither — it lives in createPartnerTheme.ts, a third file. Re-reading all three under standing rule 6 surfaced it.

flag.summary: The desktop nav bar is 76.8px, not 65px — the inline patient search column is taller than the 65px icon buttons and sets the Toolbar height.
flag.where: navigation-ui/src/components/PatientSearch/PatientSearch.tsx wrapper Box p:2 and TextField sx, against Navigation.tsx Toolbar sx minHeight:64.
flag.detail: Derivation, every term from source: InputBase input height 1.4375em = 23px (InputBase.js:127, boxSizing content-box) + OutlinedInput size-small padding 8.5px top and bottom (OutlinedInput.js:113) = 40px input; + the PatientSearch sx "&& .MuiInputBase-root { padding: 0.3 }" = 0.3 x 8 = 2.4px each side = 44.8px; + the wrapper Box p:2 = 16px each side = 76.8px. The Toolbar is align-items:center with only a minHeight floor, so its height is max(left cluster 65, right cluster 76.8) = 76.8. Below sm the inline search is not rendered (isInlineSearchVisible = isSmUp) and the bar falls back to 65px.
flag.whyItWasMissed: Two passes read the Toolbar and the icon button and stopped there. The height is actually set by a component in a different package folder that neither pass opened.
flag.handling: Figma is built at 76.8px. Both breakpoint heights recorded on the Nav / Bar description.
flag.correction: The arithmetic was right and the conclusion was wrong. Summing the search wrapper's 32px padding onto the 44.8px field assumed the toolbar stacks its children's box heights; a flex toolbar with align-items:center centres them instead. The search column never forces the bar to 76.8 — it centres inside whatever height the bar is. Rendered product is 65px. Superseded by components.PrimaryNavBar.geometryRuling (Daniel, product-rendered authority).
flag.lesson: A derivation can be arithmetically sound and still describe something that never renders. For layout that depends on flex behaviour, the rendered product outranks the computation.

flag.summary: The nav surfaced the first authored-fractional dimensions in the build; resolved by rounding to whole numbers with the computed value recorded.
flag.where: Nav / Bar 1440x76.8, Nav / Search 400x76.8 with a 44.8px field, Nav / Logo 100x23.88, Icon / Payments inner glyph 24x18.24.
flag.detail: Three independent sources, none of them an authoring choice. (1) The 0.3 spacing multiplier in PatientSearch's TextField sx resolves to 2.4px and propagates to 44.8 and 76.8. (2) The Tebra wordmark's viewBox ratio 186.82/782.49 at the declared 100px width gives 23.88. (3) PaymentsIcon's 25x19 viewBox in a 24x24 box gives 18.24. Every previous fractional value in this build was a pxToRem inflation with an intended integer behind it, which the rule handles by binding the integer and recording computedPx. These have no intended integer — the fraction IS the value.
flag.handling: Resolved. No further height or geometry archaeology on the nav; the investigation is frozen. The sub-sm bar height stays 65px and is exact.
flag.resolution: Daniel, as design authority, ruled on 2026-08-03: round each fractional value to its nearest integer and record the true computed value as computedPx, per the same convention already used for pxToRem inflation. Applied — bar 76.8 -> 77, search column 76.8 -> 77, search field 44.8 -> 45, search text inset 16.4 -> 16, wordmark 23.88 -> 24, Payments glyph 18.24 -> 18 at y 2.88 -> 3. The allDimensionsInteger invariant is restored file-wide. This is recorded as a DESIGNED DECISION (source: Daniel, this pass), not a transcription — the Figma values are deliberately not the computed values, and every departure is documented in the component description and here.
flag.amendment: The standing rule is amended rather than broken: authored-fractional sources get ROUNDED-WITH-RECORD, not preserved. Previously the rule only contemplated pxToRem inflation, where an intended integer existed behind the fraction. It now covers the case where no intended integer exists — the fraction is still not carried into Figma, and computedPx still carries the truth.
